transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-28
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Liam (Equinox VP Eng), Sana (ML Platform Lead), Dev (SRE), Hannah (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick QBR-style check-in; focus on offboarding pilot to production, pricing conversation, and technical benchmarking.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, i'll run the agenda quick — 1) pilot offboarding plan / economic adjustments, 2) latency benchmarks and SE follow-up, 3) security and kms questions, 4) next steps. sound good?

[00:18] Liam: yeah sounds good — we'll, we'll mostly be listening but Sana and Dev have the details.

[00:25] Sana: hi — quick context, pilot has been running for 5 weeks, roughly 1.2MM tokens/day, a lot of short user queries but a long-tail of long prompts for dispute cases. overall happy with quality but cost is creeping.

[00:42] Maya: totally expected — thanks. Arjun i'll hand over to you to summarize latency and the outlier distribution you saw in the report.

[00:48] Arjun: yeah thanks. so, key point — 95th pct is what we've been watching. median is fine ~80-100ms token latency in host mode for the short requests, but the 95th jumps to ~750-1,000ms during concurrent bursts. We dug into KV cache warmup — because you have mix of short and long sequences, cache misses on the longer flows cause tail spikes. also saw a few retry storms from client-side timeout settings enumerating requests.

[01:15] Dev: when you say KV cache warmup, is that on your side or ours? i think some of it is from our session tokenization.

[01:22] Arjun: it's primarily runtime KV cache in the model serving layer — when a long sequence opens a new context for a user, the backend is fetching and building the key-value layers. on Redwood Dedicated we can pre-warm with pinned sessions or reuse schema which reduces those spikes. the other lever is batching windows — tiny windows help latency but increase cost, larger windows amortize compute.

[01:46] Hannah: cost is the thing — can you show the committed usage discount breakpoints again?

[01:52] Maya: yeah i'll send the updated pricing doc after today. high-level: a 30% committed tier at 500k tokens/day effective reduces unit to around X (we'll send exact numbers). also we can apply burst capacity discounts for first 6 weeks after switching to Dedicated.

[02:10] Liam: okay good — timeline wise we're aiming to be fully on Dedicated by mid-November, legal needs some SOC2 details first.

[02:18] Maya: understood — we'll get our SOC2 type II package and AICPA contact. Arjun, maybe you can cover network and KMS notes?

[02:25] Arjun: sure. for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) — you can bring keys and we keep only encrypted pointers in the control plane. For VPC peering we recommend a dedicated subnet and egress rules to the model fleet. audit logs are available per-request and can be pushed to your S3 or SIEM.

[02:45] Sana: good, that aligns. legal asked specifically about HSM-backed keys and whether Redwood holds any plaintext during model inference.

[02:52] Arjun: no plaintext is stored; inference happens in the runtime with ephemeral memory. keys are used for decrypting model artifacts and for metadata encryption. we can provide the whitepaper and HSM integration docs.

[03:05] Dev: one question — how long do you keep logs by default? we have to meet PGD retention windows for disputes.

[03:12] Maya: by default hosted retains 30 days, Dedicated is configurable up to 365 days as an addon. we'll note that in the offboarding checklist.

[03:20] Liam: ok. let's talk about the benchmark next — Arjun what's the plan to reproduce our production-like QPS in staging?

[03:28] Arjun: plan is: you give us a 24-hour sample of request traces (anonymized), we'll run a 2-hour stress window that mimics your qps and seq length histogram at 3 different concurrency levels. we will capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, memory usage, kernel saturation, and retry rates. propose to run next Tuesday morning in your timezone.

[03:48] Sana: we'll anonymize and send that by Friday.

[03:52] Arjun: perfect. note — when you send traces include tokenization artifacts; we saw your client library does some pre-tokenization for dispute flows which alters seq length.

[04:05] Maya: back to costs — we also noticed some high-cost patterns related to proactive logging and debug context in requests. are there any quick wins?

[04:13] Dev: yeah we currently attach full user history to every request for context. we can probably reduce that; product asked for it to improve continuity.

[04:20] Hannah: it's a product tradeoff, but if we can reduce retention of history for certain flows that might drop avg tokens by 20%.

[04:28] Arjun: additional levers: prefix caching (we can cache common templates), quantized model variant for non-sensitive flows (4-bit quantization) which lowers cost per token and slightly increases latency but within acceptable bounds for chat.

[04:42] Liam: question about quality regression if we use quantized model for some paths — do you have monitoring for that?

[04:49] Arjun: yes we can run evaluation suites as part of rollout, Redwood Optimize can run A/B with automatic rollback if quality drops above thresholds you set. we recommended a small canary (5-10% traffic) for 2 weeks.

[05:02] Sana: good — for the legal team we also need an outline of the rollback policy and who is the point-of-contact for incident response.

[05:10] Maya: we'll include that in the offboarding doc and list on-call contacts from Redwood.
transcript_continued:
[05:18] Liam: how do cost reconciliations look post pilot — any surprises?

[05:24] Maya: main surprise was bursty long-seq requests during the dispute batch that spiked tail costs. switching to Dedicated + KV pre-warm and batching helped model-side costs but the client-side retry loops were compounding it.

[05:36] Dev: note that some of our retry logic is aggressive — we will revise thresholds and backoff.

[05:40] Arjun: also, we saw a spectral pattern where certain hours had sudden token spikes — looks like a backend job that expanded datasets — if you can schedule those jobs outside peak it helps.

[05:54] Hannah: product question — once we move to Dedicated, how quickly can we change model variants if a newer model appears?

[06:02] Arjun: model rollout is governed by your pinned version and rollout policy. Typical timeline to onboard a new model variant and test is 2-3 weeks for regression evals and canary. but if you want faster we can accelerate with an expanded eval track.

[06:18] Liam: legal again — about data residency, our EU users must keep logs in region. can Dedicated be region-locked?

[06:26] Maya: yes Dedicated can be provisioned in regionally isolated capacity. Private deployments are the more strict option for full on-prem or VPC-only access. We'll map options in the offboarding checklist.

[06:38] Sana: about SLAs — our ops needs 99.9 uptime and a clearly defined MTTR. do you have that on Dedicated?

[06:45] Maya: we offer SLA-backed uptime on Dedicated with an SLO and credits schedule. we'll include the specific SLA text in the packet.

[06:52] Liam: ok great. next, a short recap of operational handoff?

[06:58] Maya: yes. step one — pilot offboarding: sign committed usage, schedule staging benchmark, legal review SOC2/HSM, finalize KMS, finalize retention. step two — provision Dedicated fleet and run soak. step three — hand to CSM for adoption.

[07:14] Hannah: when do you need signatures for committed usage?

[07:18] Maya: ideal would be by Oct 10 to hit the mid-November Dedicated date. but flexible if legal needs more time.

[07:24] Sana: we'll aim for Oct 8 internal signoff.

[07:28] Dev: about the benchmark data — is there anything sensitive we should redact?

[07:32] Arjun: remove PII, keep request timing and token lengths. we only need histograms and representative payload shapes.

[07:40] Maya: a couple small product asks — can Redwood add a per-route cost tag in the console so we can attribute cost to dispute flows vs conversational flows?

[07:49] Arjun: yes that's on the roadmap and we can enable a trial tag for you; we'll export cost per route and token metric.

[07:56] Liam: nice. any other blockers?

[08:00] Sana: legal wants encryption-at-rest proof and a named security contact.

[08:05] Maya: we'll send security contact and the encryption proof in the package.

[08:10] Arjun: quick note on the benchmark: we'll try two configurations — (A) tighter batching to prioritize latency at the cost of compute, (B) larger batch windows for cost reduction. we'll show delta.

[08:22] Dev: can you share the expected delta numbers up front?

[08:26] Arjun: rough ballpark — variant A p95 ~250-400ms, variant B p95 ~700-1,000ms but cost per token ~20-35% lower for B. exact numbers depend on your seq len histogram.

[08:40] Hannah: okay that's helpful.

[08:44] Maya: last item — can we lock a date for the Dedicated provisioning dry run?

[08:48] Liam: mid-November works for production, dry run maybe Nov 1?

[08:52] Maya: Nov 1 dry run penciled — we'll set a follow-up invite.

[08:58] Hannah: thanks everyone, this was helpful.

[09:02] Maya: quick recap of next steps verbally — i'll send pricing and the offboarding doc, Arjun will run the benchmarks next week with traces you send, Sana/Dev confirm KMS and retention, and we'll set the dry run for Nov 1.

[09:18] Liam: thanks Maya and Arjun, talk soon.

[09:22] Meeting end.
